questions.content: In Insertion Sort, values from the unsorted part are picked and placed into the sorted part. Which of the following best describes how an element from the unsorted part is integrated into the sorted part?
options: It is always swapped with the first element of the sorted part.
It is always appended to the end of the sorted part.
It is shifted through the sorted part until its correct position is found.
It is compared only with the last element of the sorted part.

questions.content: Selection Sort always places the smallest element found in the unsorted portion at the current iteration's sorted position.
Briefly describe the 'Divide and Conquer' strategy as applied to sorting algorithms, outlining its three main conceptual steps.
questions.answer: divide the array into sorted and unsorted portions, recursively add portions of the unsorted to the sorted

grading.expected: divide the array into sorted and unsorted portions, recursively add portions of the unsorted to the sorted

questions.content: Mergesort is a recursive algorithm. What is the base case for the recursion in Mergesort's 'divide' step?
options: When the array is entirely sorted.
When the sub-array has 0 or 1 element.
When the sub-array length is less than 5.
When the sub-arrays are of equal size.

questions.content: The merging process in Mergesort typically requires an auxiliary array to temporarily hold elements while combining the sorted sub-arrays.
During the merging step of Mergesort, how does the algorithm decide which element from the two sorted halves to place next into the auxiliary array?
questions.answer: the pointer to the current unsorted element

grading.expected: the pointer to the current unsorted element

questions.content: What is the primary function of the 'pivot' element in Quicksort?
options: To be the smallest element in the entire list.
To divide the list into two sub-lists: elements less than it and elements greater than it.
To be exchanged with the largest element in the list.
To mark the end of the sorted portion of the array.

questions.content: Quicksort's average time complexity is O(n log n), but its worst-case scenario can lead to O(n^2) time complexity.
Explain why consistently choosing the left-most element as the pivot in Quicksort can lead to its worst-case time complexity, especially for already-sorted arrays.
questions.answer: because then you aren't pivoting anything

grading.expected: because then you aren't pivoting anything

questions.content: Which of the following conditions contributes to Quicksort's performance degrading to its worst-case O(n^2) time complexity?
options: Always picking a pivot that splits the array into nearly equal halves.
Using an auxiliary array during partitioning.
Choosing a pivot that consistently results in highly unbalanced partitions.
The presence of only unique elements in the array.
